title: The Kanban board, embedded live from its own port
summary: `kanban-loop` is an own-port Fitting — it serves its own React board on its own HTTP port, not as a faculty-tab view. Opening `/fitting/kanban-loop` lands on the dynamic catch-all shim, but the live board is embedded at `/embed/kanban-loop`, which reads the Fitting's status file under `~/.garrison/ui-fittings`, resolves a URL the *remote* browser can actually reach (loopback locally, the HTTPS tailnet endpoint over Tailscale), and renders the board in an iframe instead of raw JSON — falling back to an honest 'not running' / 'not published' message when it can't.

states.label: Kanban view
states.description: The drillbook asks that the embedded Kanban surface load the visual workflow board rather than raw JSON, and that the board stay navigable and legible without destructive overflow. Because `kanban-loop` is an own-port Fitting, the board isn't a component Garrison renders — it's a separate React app on its own port, and this flow is the plumbing that reaches it from wherever the operator's browser happens to be.

steps.title: The /fitting route is a one-line shim onto the surface panel
steps.description: Every `/fitting/<id>[/<rest>]` URL is served by one dynamic catch-all page that does nothing but mount `FittingSurfacePanel`. For an own-port Fitting like `kanban-loop` this page renders only a status/controls strip — the real board lives on the Fitting's own port and embeds at `/embed/kanban-loop`, which the rest of this flow follows.

next.label: status comes from the ui-fittings dir

steps.title: The server reads the Fitting's status file and probes it live
steps.description: The one source of truth for an own-port view is its JSON file under `~/.garrison/ui-fittings`, written when the Fitting starts and removed on SIGTERM. The API reads each file, then decides live-vs-down by probing `<url>/health` *server-side* — own-port Fittings emit no CORS headers, so a browser probe always fails — and attaches the port's `tailscale serve` mapping as `tailnetUrl` so a remote client can reach it over HTTPS.

steps.title: The embed page fetches status and gates on running-vs-down
steps.description: `/embed/kanban-loop` fetches the same views feed with `cache: "no-store"` and finds its own entry. If the Fitting has no entry or no URL, the board simply isn't up — the page says so and tells the operator to start the operative, rather than rendering a broken frame. Only a running Fitting with a URL falls through to URL resolution.

steps.title: Resolve a URL the actual browser can reach
steps.description: The status file's `url` is a loopback address (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>`) — correct for the server's own health probe, wrong for a browser reached over Tailscale, where localhost is the *user's* device. `resolveViewUrl` picks by page host: loopback locally, the same-host HTTPS `tailnetUrl` over the tailnet. Its load-bearing guard is the last branch — on an HTTPS page it returns `""` rather than an `http://` URL, because a plain-HTTP iframe on an HTTPS page is blocked as mixed content and would silently render blank.

next.label: render the board (or explain the gap)

steps.title: The board renders in an iframe, not raw JSON
steps.description: With a reachable base URL the page embeds the Fitting's own React board in a full-height iframe — the visual workflow board the drillbook wants, not a JSON dump. Query params are forwarded so a deep-linked card survives. When `resolveViewUrl` returned `""` (running but no tailnet mapping), the code just above this renders a 'not published to the tailnet' explainer with a Publish button instead of a blank pane — so the surface is always either the live board or an honest reason it isn't.
